query: I stopped by the community park on my walk home earlier today, and the whole place smelled like the fresh-cut clover and honey-sweet clover blooms that pop up right around this time every year. There was a tiny golden retriever puppy zooming back and forth off-leash near the picnic tables, tripping over its own floppy paws every few steps while its owner laughed and tried to corral it back to their blanket. A group of teen girls was spread out on a faded tie-dye tapestry passing around a container of neon pink lemonade, and one of them was playing soft, scratchy indie folk on a beat-up portable speaker that kept cutting out when the wind picked up. I hung around leaning against an oak tree for almost 20 minutes just watching everything, and it made the whole gray, drizzly start to the morning feel totally worth it. All of my go-to skincare picks are totally cruelty free, and I always keep an eye out for that key ingredient I always look for in my skincare stuff, you know the one I mean? I stick to that usual limit I keep for drugstore beauty buys for my budget, so anything way over that never ends up in my basket. I’ve heard there are great makeup remover options that line up with all of those markers, too.
